title: Zone-aware subnet lifecycle operator for private VPCs
creator: Ava Thompson
description:
Goal: Build a Terraform module and small operator (Terraform-runbook + controller) that manages zone-aware subnet lifecycle and egress primitives for Private (VPC) deployments. The operator should: 1) provision AZ-aligned subnet groups and attach NAT/IGW placements per availability zone when required, 2) reconcile and rotate VPC endpoints (S3, SecretsManager, KMS) with target route table associations, 3) expose health probes and synthetic checks for subnet/egress reachability used by deployment automation and upgrade canaries, and 4) provide safe upgrade primitives (canary apply, drift detection, rollback hooks) to avoid cross-AZ outage during Terraform-driven upgrades.

Scope: Implement Terraform module with opinionated defaults for private workloads, a small controller script (Go or Python) that runs post-apply checks and can trigger canary rollouts, and examples + CI pipelines. Deliverables: terraform module (variables/outputs/docs), controller binary/script in infra repo, canary plan and test harness, dashboards for synthetic probe results, and an upgrade playbook.

Acceptance criteria:
- Module supports multi-AZ subnets with naming conventions and tagging consistent with Redwood standards.
- Option to place NAT gateways or use centralized egress with explicit failover routing.
- VPC endpoints created with policy attachments and route table associations per subnet-group.
- Module emits metrics/outputs used by the operator: subnet IDs, route table IDs, endpoint IDs, nat/igw placements.
- Synthetic reachability tests (lambda or ephemeral runner) run post-apply and surface results to internal dashboard.
- Upgrade flow supports canary applies to 1 AZ and an automated rollback when health probes fail.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- We will prefer per-AZ NAT gateways when low-latency egress is required, but expose a centralised egress pattern for cost-sensitive customers. This increases Terraform complexity (conditional resources) but gives customer choice.
- Using an external short-lived controller reduces the need to implement a long-running Kubernetes operator; the controller will be invoked by CI or Terragrunt hooks after terraform apply. If adoption requires it later we can migrate to a k8s operator.
- Route table associations are managed idempotently; we will avoid destructive route replacement during canary upgrades by creating new route tables and swapping associations in a controlled sequence.
- Security: VPC endpoints include resource policies referencing account IDs and enforced tags. KMS endpoints require review; flagging security_review_required=true for this ticket.

Files & interfaces planned:
- modules/vpc-zone-subnets/{main.tf,variables.tf,outputs.tf,README.md} with examples/central-egress.tf and examples/per-az-nat.tf
- infra/tools/vpc-health-controller/{cmd,tests,bin-release} - lightweight binary invoked by CI
- ci/terragrunt/hooks/post_apply_health_check.yaml - wired into apply pipeline
- docs/private-vpc/upgrade-playbook.md and docs/private-vpc/canary-runbook.md

Outputs expected from module (string outputs for downstream automation): subnet_groups, route_table_map, nat_placements, endpoint_map, module_revision_tag
